Title: Main Debugging Detective
Role: Your task is to find the buggy method. You have static tools to read code and a special dynamic verification tool.

Workflow:
1. Prioritize Error Analysis: If a stack trace is provided, start by investigating the deepest method in the trace that belongs to the target project. This is often where the bug or the symptom manifests.
2. Static Exploration: Use static tools (get_code_snippet, etc.) to read the code at the identified suspicious locations. Pay close attention to variable calculations and boundary conditions (especially for IndexOutOfBounds errors).
3. Hypothesis Formulation: Form a specific hypothesis about the root cause (e.g., "Line 95 performs a double increment on the index, causing an overflow").
4. Dynamic Verification (Recommended): Call `nominate_suspicious_method` to verify your hypothesis with runtime data.
   - Specify `variables_of_interest` that are involved in the failing condition (e.g., loop counters, index variables, or null-check targets).
   - The sub-agent will provide ground-truth runtime values to confirm or refute your hypothesis.
   - If the verification report says NO_BUG or INCONCLUSIVE, consider investigating other methods or re-nominating with different `target_lines`.
   - You may nominate multiple methods if you have several plausible hypotheses.

Goal: Provide the final diagnosis based on the available evidence (static and/or dynamic).

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The test `['com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInferenceTest.testNoThisInference()']` failed.
The test looks like:

```java
1000 :   public void testNoThisInference() {
1001 :     JSType thisType = createNullableType(OBJECT_TYPE);
1002 :     assumingThisType(thisType);
1003 :     inFunction("var out = 3; if (goog.isNull(this)) out = this;"); // error occurred here
1005 :   }
```

It failed with the following error message and call stack:

```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Node cannot be refined. 
THIS 1 [source_file: [testcode]] : Object
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.declareNameInScope(ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.java:175)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.restrictParameter(ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.java:239)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.java:220)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(TypeInference.java:235)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(TypeInference.java:64)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis$BranchedForwardDataFlowAnalysis.flow(DataFlowAnalysis.java:447)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(DataFlowAnalysis.java:212)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(DataFlowAnalysis.java:180)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInferenceTest.inFunction(TypeInferenceTest.java:126)
	at com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInferenceTest.testNoThisInference(TypeInferenceTest.java:1003)
```

Start by calling the `get_failing_tests_covered_classes` function.

[".branchedFlowThrough(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".traverse(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".getJSType(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".getPropertyType(com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType, java.lang.String, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".updateScopeForTypeChange(com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType)", ".TypeInference(com.google.javascript.jscomp.AbstractCompiler, com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph<com.google.javascript.rhino.Node>, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.ReverseAbstractInterpreter, com.google.javascript.jscomp.Scope, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodingConvention.AssertionFunctionSpec>)", ".tightenTypesAfterAssertions(com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".traverseCall(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".redeclareSimpleVar(com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType)", ".isUnflowable(com.google.javascript.jscomp.Scope.Var)", ".traverseName(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".traverseGetProp(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".dereferencePointer(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".getNativeType(com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSTypeNative)", ".traverseChildren(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)", ".createInitialEstimateLattice()", ".createEntryLattice()", ".flowThrough(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope)"]

The failure is caused by a mismatch between what the reverse abstract interpreter treats as a “qualified/refinable” expression and what it can actually refine in scope.

Diagnosis:
- In `ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(...)`, the code accepts any argument `param` where `param.isQualifiedName()` is true.
- In Rhino, `Node.isQualifiedName()` returns `true` for `Token.THIS`.
- So for the condition `goog.isNull(this)`, the interpreter proceeds to refine `this`.
- `ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.getTypeIfRefinable(...)` does not explicitly handle `Token.THIS`, so it returns `null` or allows the path to continue based on surrounding logic.
- Then `ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.restrictParameter(...)` calls `declareNameInScope(...)` on that `THIS` node.
- But `ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.declareNameInScope(...)` only supports `NAME` and `GETPROP`, and throws for everything else. `THIS` falls into the default branch, producing:
  `IllegalArgumentException: Node cannot be refined.`

So the buggy behavior is that `ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter` treats `this` as refinable because it relies on `isQualifiedName()`, but `ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.declareNameInScope(...)` explicitly cannot refine `this`.

Most likely root cause:
- `ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.jscomp.type.FlowScope, boolean)`
- specifically the guard `param.isQualifiedName()` is too broad for reverse type refinement, because it includes `THIS`.

A safer expected behavior would be to skip refinement for `THIS` (consistent with the comment in `declareNameInScope`: `"this" references aren't currently modeled in the CFG.`).

SYSTEM ALERT: You explained your thoughts but did not output a valid tool call. 
- If you need to examine code or verify a hypothesis, you MUST explicitly invoke a function (e.g., `get_code_snippet`, `nominate_suspicious_method`).
- If you have completely finished the investigation and are ready to provide the final buggy method signature, reply EXACTLY with the word 'READY'.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(Node, FlowScope, boolean)
ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreter.restrictParameter(Node, JSType, FlowScope, Function, boolean)
ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.declareNameInScope(FlowScope, Node, JSType)
